responsibility.value: Read-only access to rentals for both students and store staff: single-rental lookups and paged/search listings, with billing figures computed on the fly for every returned DTO.

Owns: Mapping InstrumentRental entities to InstrumentRentalDto and attaching computed billing fields via RentalBilling
Student-scoped filtering for GetByIdForStudentAsync / GetPagedForStudentAsync (filters by StudentProfile.AppUserId == actor.UserId)
doesNotOwn: Store-scoped filtering for the store-facing queries — GetByIdForStoreAsync and GetPagedForStoreAsync do not filter by the caller's store at all
Billing calculation logic — delegated to RentalBilling
Write access — this service is read-only, no state mutation

collaborators.detail: Used only in the student-facing methods to scope by AppUserId
Applied to every DTO before it's returned

contracts: GetByIdForStudentAsync and GetPagedForStudentAsync only ever return rentals owned by the calling student (AppUserId filter is applied at the query level, not in memory).
GetByIdForStoreAsync and GetPagedForStoreAsync return matching rentals across ALL stores with no MusicStoreId filter applied in this class — tenant scoping for these two methods is not enforced here.
Every returned DTO has billing fields populated as of 'now' at query time — billing is not cached or stale.
assumptions: Callers of GetByIdForStoreAsync / GetPagedForStoreAsync are expected to already be scoped to their own store by a controller-level filter or middleware before reaching this service — the class itself does not verify or restrict by MusicStoreId.
actor.UserId reflects the currently authenticated student and cannot be spoofed by the caller.
failureModes: NotFoundException when a lookup by id matches no row (or matches a row outside the caller's own scope for the student-facing methods, which is indistinguishable from not existing — same exception, so no ownership is leaked).
Silent over-broad results for the store-facing methods if a scoping filter is missing upstream — this is a data-exposure risk, not a thrown exception.
architecturalNotes: This is the counterpart flagged by the external blast-radius review as the tenant-isolation risk point: GetByIdForStoreAsync and GetPagedForStoreAsync are unscoped by design (CQRS read-side keeps scoping in the controller/middleware layer), but that means a missing or buggy upstream filter is a direct cross-tenant data leak with no defense-in-depth at this layer.
GetPagedForStudentAsync / GetPagedForStoreAsync differ only in the base IQueryable passed to GetPagedAsync — the shared paging/search/billing pipeline is common to both.
